newsitem.title: USA: Chicago suburb eyes $5.3 mln school bonds - paper.
newsitem.headline: Chicago suburb eyes $5.3 mln school bonds - paper.

text.p: Residents of an affluent north suburban Chicago school district will be asked to approve a $5.3 million bond referendum in November to eliminate a deficit and bolster operating revenues, the Chicago Sun-Times reported Tuesday.

Wilmette school officials voted on Monday night to seek the referendum, the newspaper said. The proposal also needs signatures of 10 percent of residents who voted in the last general election to be placed on the November ballot, the newspaper said.
Voters narrowly rejected a proposed property tax increase in April that would have accomplished the same goals, the newspaper said.
Proceeds from the debt issuance would go to the district's working cash fund and money in that fund would be transferred to cover a $1.1 million debt in the education fund, the newspaper said.
